parsed.doc_summary: Legal Aid Society of San Diego fact sheet (updated 2023-09-21) on the City of San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance (just cause, relocation assistance, buyout rules), effective 2023-06-24. Only just-cause category is supported; no rent cap, deposit, fee or screening rules stated.

rules.title: San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance (just cause, relocation assistance, buyout rules)
rules.requirement: Landlords may terminate covered tenancies only for at-fault or no-fault just cause, must state the cause in the notice, and must pay relocation assistance (2 months' rent, or 3 for seniors/disabled tenants) for no-fault terminations. Buyout agreements must follow disclosure and form rules, and retaliation is barred.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§§ 98.0701 et seq.)
citation_aliases: City of San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.
rules.effective_date_note: Fact sheet states the Ordinance goes into effect June 24, 2023; indefinite unless amended.
rules.key_value: Relocation: 2 months' rent (3 months if tenant is 62+ or disabled) for no-fault terminations
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies (right to occupy more than 30 days) in residential rental units, including mobilehome park rentals.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing (not for Section 8 voucher holders); transient hotels; short-term occupancy of 30 days or less; mobilehomes subject to MRL; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; school-owned dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner; owner-occupied single-family renting up to 2 units/rooms; owner-occupied duplex; separately alienable units such as condos owned by non-corporate/non-REIT landlords with written exemption notice; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive/equitable relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x required relocation assistance plus actual damages for nonpayment; attorney's fees.
rules.interaction: Consistent with and more protective than Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2; notice mentions Civ. Code § 1947.12.

unverifiable_exemptions: condo/separately alienable unit owned by non-corporate, non-REIT landlord with exemption notice
nonprofit, religious, hospital or care facilities
